exact_source_scope: Axiomatic Definition section; NOT circular initial or uncorrected digit-sequence formulations
definition_context: Real-number system as a Dedekind complete totally ordered field
independently_paraphrased_definition: A real-number system is a field R equipped with a total order ≤ compatible with translation and multiplication by positive elements, such that every nonempty A⊆R bounded above has a least upper bound in R. Such ordered field systems are unique up to ordered-field isomorphism, rather than as literally equal underlying sets.
mathematical_rigor_decision: Axiomatically sound. The article first describes reals as rationals plus irrationals, explicitly admits that description is circular, and later gives the complete ordered-field axioms; use ONLY the latter as the definition. Cauchy classes and Dedekind-cut constructions are alternative realizations that require separate rigorous source screening.
context_specific_variants: Cauchy sequence equivalence classes of rationals
potential_new_relations: real absolute value→complete ordered real field
real complete ordered field→totally ordered field

exact_source_scope: Totally Ordered Field subsection, not general partially ordered field subsection
definition_context: Field with total order compatible with addition and multiplication by strictly positive scalars
independently_paraphrased_definition: A totally ordered field is a field F with a total order ≤ such that x<y implies x+z<y+z for any z∈F, and x<y with z>0 implies xz<yz. No Dedekind completeness is assumed.
mathematical_rigor_decision: Retain the totality qualifier; ProofWiki distinguishes a general partially ordered field from a totally ordered field and notes variable authorial naming. Rational numbers with the usual order are a totally ordered field but not Dedekind complete.
context_specific_variants: totally ordered field with field-compatible total order
partially ordered field is broader and source conventions vary
potential_new_relations: complete ordered real field→totally ordered field

exact_source_scope: Definition:Dedekind Completeness Property, also labeled least-upper-bound property
definition_context: Order theory: Dedekind completeness of a poset via bounded nonempty subsets
independently_paraphrased_definition: An ordered set S is Dedekind complete if every nonempty subset A of S with at least one upper bound in S has a least upper bound (supremum) belonging to S.
mathematical_rigor_decision: Source states order-theoretic supremum property; it is not metric completeness nor the statement every Cauchy sequence converges in a general ordered set. For Archimedean ordered fields the familiar completeness characterizations need separate equivalence proof.
context_specific_variants: corresponding infimum property by order duality
not equivalent to arbitrary metric completeness without further hypotheses

exact_source_scope: Piecewise absolute-value definition and nonnegative square-root representation
definition_context: Real ordered-field absolute value and its equivalent nonnegative square-root expression
independently_paraphrased_definition: For a real number x, define |x|=x when x≥0 and |x|=−x when x<0; equivalently |x|=sqrt(x²), where the square root denotes the unique nonnegative root. The latter equivalence uses completeness/existence of nonnegative real square roots.
mathematical_rigor_decision: Retain order compatibility and the sign case split; no general norm on arbitrary vector spaces is implied. The sqrt form is an equivalent variant for nonnegative squares in reals, but not a primary algebraic axiom.
context_specific_variants: piecewise definition by order (elementary educational order)
potential_new_relations: absolute value of real number→real complete ordered field
